input: It is recommended that the capital decision should be held at this stage and that a metered trial should instead be run on one of the three refrigeration lines, with the plant engineer taking ownership of the trial. The background is that a food plant currently uses 2167 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration. A heat-recovery retrofit has been proposed, and the equipment vendor projects that it would save 14% of that annual use. This corresponds to a derived saving of 303 MWh per year at the vendor figure. The capital cost of the retrofit is $491k. Using an electricity price of $0.11 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $33k, and the derived simple payback is 14.9 years. The derived figures are 303 MWh per year, $33k per year, and a payback of 14.9 years on the stated capital cost. In simple terms, the trade-off can be summarised as $491k of capital set against $33k of derived annual saving. It is important to note, however, that the saving is a vendor projection and has not been measured at this plant. A further limitation is that refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the annual figures should not be taken as a complete picture of performance under peak conditions. Overall, a metered trial on one line is presented as a prudent intermediate step, because it would provide measured evidence from the plant itself before any final capital commitment is made.
target: Hold the capital decision and run a metered trial on one of the three refrigeration lines. The plant engineer owns the trial. A food plant uses 2167 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration, and that annual use is the evidence base for the figures that follow. A heat-recovery retrofit is projected by the equipment vendor to save 14% of that use, a derived saving of 303 MWh per year at the vendor figure. Capital cost is $491k. At an electricity price of $0.11 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $33k and the derived simple payback is 14.9 years. The trade-off is $491k of capital against $33k of derived annual saving, with the saving projected by the vendor and not measured at this plant. The derived labels matter. The 303 MWh saving is derived from the vendor percentage applied to the stated annual use; the $33k annual saving is derived from the electricity price; and the 14.9-year payback is derived from the capital cost and the annual saving. Refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled. The annual figures therefore do not settle the retrofit's value in the peak month, and the passage makes no peak-month claim. A metered trial on a single line gives plant measurement in place of the vendor projection before capital is committed. The trial is also the only step in the summary that changes the evidence. The other figures are arithmetic on stated values: a percentage applied to annual use, a price applied to saved energy, and a payback formed from cost and saving. Measurement on one line tests the vendor percentage where the plant's own refrigeration duty is concerned, without first committing the capital that the payback calculation already makes difficult to justify on the vendor case. The recommendation is the trial, under the plant engineer, not approval of the retrofit.
